explanation: Measure both lengths and advance the longer list by their difference. Then move the two pointers together until their node references coincide or both reach the end.
timeComplexity: O(m+n) Two length scans and aligned traversal visit O(m+n) links.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Lengths and traversal pointers use constant storage.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/DoTerminatedListsOverlap.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: After equalizing remaining lengths, both pointers are equally far from their tails. If a shared tail exists, they reach its first shared node together; otherwise they reach null together. Reference comparison distinguishes true sharing from equal values.
walkthrough: Prefixes [1] and [2,3] share [8,9]. Advance the longer second list once, then move together: both pointers reach the same node 8, which is returned. The executable case’s true result is the judge adapter verdict; the callable returns the tree/node/list of moves/random sample described above.
edgeCases: Two empty lists overlap at no node and return null.
A shared suffix may begin at one head.
Equal Data values without shared references are disjoint.
